Derive a beta prior for an AE from an homogeneous set of historical studies.

Source: R/chi_squ_prior.R
chi_squ_prior.Rd

The historical studies are assumed to be heterogeneous. That assumption is tested using sequential chi-squared tests. If homogeneity is detected, the largest outlier study is removed from the historical set and the test rerun. This cycle continues until: i) heterogeneity is not rejected; or ii) there is only one historical study remaining.

Usage

chi_squ_prior(y, n, time, time_std = 1, alpha = 0.01, verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

y

numeric vector, number of events in the trials.

n

numeric vector, number of patients in the trials (either the total sample size or effective sample size, see Details for more information).

time

numeric vector, strictly positive, time at risk in the trials.

time_std

numeric, the unit of time we standardize to.

alpha

the one-sided percentile to use in the chi-squared test of heterogeneity.

verbose

logical, TRUE to see log messages about heterogeneous studies being dropped.

Value

a list with elements alpha and beta, the shape parameters of a beta distribution that defines the prior.

Details

It is recommended to use the total number of events in the trial (one event per subject is counted) and effective sample size (the number of subjects who completed the study plus fractional dropouts) as the number of patients in the trial (n). The planned study duration of the blinded ongoing study is used for standardization (time_std).

Examples

y <- c(10, 300, 0)
n <- c(95, 1050, 5)
time <- c(1, 3, 0.1)
chi_squ_prior(y = y, n = n, time = time)
#> $alpha
#> [1] 121.4013
#> 
#> $beta
#> [1] 1028.599
#>
